payload.author: exam:3@run-18
payload.body:
examiner (exam-3): writing `tests/lint-ui.test.ts` as five `test` blocks, one per Proof leg, each named for its leg and its Machine clause.

Shape: one memoised probe writes the three temporary files under a single module-level random suffix — the component at `client/src/components/ui/lint-ui-tmp-<rand>.tsx`, the sample at `client/src/lint-ui-tmp-<rand>/Bad.tsx` and the copy at `client/src/components/ui/lint-ui-tmp-<rand>-bad.tsx`, each from the verbatim Proof fence — runs both commands (`node node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js --print-config <sample>` for leg b, `bun run lint:ui -f json` for legs c/d/e) and removes them in a `finally`. Legs (c), (d) and (e) read the *same* run, because (d) only means anything if the ignored copy was on the tree while (c)'s entry was produced. `client/src/components/` does not exist at BASE (Task 1 creates it), so the probe records whether it was there and removes only what it created.

Two readings I am writing down:
  - Leg (c)'s "exactly one entry" is one entry *whose filePath ends with the sample path*, not one entry in the whole array: `-f json` prints one entry per linted file and the app's own seven `no-unknown-classes` findings are on the tree at this wave.
  - The JSON parse of the `bun run` stdout is guarded so that the red line at BASE names the missing script rather than a parse error — at BASE `bun run lint:ui` exits 1 with an empty stdout, which is the same exit code the leg pins, so an unguarded `JSON.parse` would have failed for a reason that reads like a typo.

payload.author: impl:2@run-18
payload.body:
Approach for task 2 (locators by role+name, aria-checked views, tailwind in bundleOf):

1. `types.ts`: add `Locator = string | {role: string; name: string}` and widen `Action`'s three arms to carry it. `actionsOf`/`isCallbackAction` are unchanged — they never read inside an action.
2. `browser.ts`: `nodeFor` becomes a resolver returning a params fragment — `{nodeId}` for a string (today's `DOM.querySelector` path) or `{backendNodeId}` for a `{role,name}` (`Accessibility.queryAXTree` on the document root, first node in tree order, `backendDOMNodeId`). `Accessibility.enable` is sent lazily, once per session, on the first object locator. `centreOf` and `DOM.focus` spread the fragment, so both paths meet at the same Input.* calls. New message: `act: no element matches role=<role> name="<name>"`; the string message stays byte-identical.
3. `render-move.ts`: `checked`/`unchecked` read `aria-checked` as well as `data-checked` (OR), so every BASE view over a reflected DOM still holds.
4. `rules/views.ts`: `readingChecked` reads the same pair, so the fix line names `#a` over a static React render that only carries `aria-checked`.
5. `bundleOf`: `plugins: [tailwind]` from `bun-plugin-tailwind`; `bun-plugin-tailwind@^0.1.2` and `tailwindcss@^4.3.3` into `packages/tinyapp-exam/package.json` dependencies, `bun install` at the root to regenerate `bun.lock`.
6. `index.ts` names `Locator` in its type export from `./types`.

`REFLECT_CHECKED` keeps to `input` elements untouched — writing `data-checked="false"` onto base-ui's span would paint shadcn's checkbox checked.

Approach — one file, legs (a)-(g): (a)+(c)+(d) read client/src/index.tsx, index.css, components.json, tsconfig.json, vite.config.js and package.json as text/JSON inside test bodies (never at module level: the linter's capture child imports this file for real, so a module-level read of a not-yet-created file would read as `capture failed` rather than as the finding it is); (b) one direct bundleOf of client/index.html asserting the three theme texts in its css; (e) four tests, one per component, each a dynamic import of ../../client/src/components/ui/<name> and a renderToStaticMarkup via React.createElement — the Proof path is .test.ts, so JSX is not available in it; (f) the single top-level stateExam of M4, id selectors only; (g) the two Run: lines spawned verbatim through bash -c from the repository root, as tests/state-exams/filter-bar.test.ts does. payload.body:
examiner (run-18 task 2), approach before writing:

Three Test: paths, each extended under a section comment naming this task; the existing legs of the two package files stay byte-identical.

- `packages/tinyapp-exam/test/browser.test.ts` — task 2 legs (a) [M1], (b) [M2], (c) [M3], (h) [M8]. Leg (a) gets two witnesses: `import type {Locator}` used in typed `Action` consts, which is what the `bunx tsc -p packages/tinyapp-exam --noEmit` Run: line grades, plus a runtime read of `src/types.ts` for `export type Locator` and for `Locator` inside the `Action` declaration (bun strips types, so a type-only import alone would be green at BASE for no reason). `actionsOf({click: {role:'checkbox',name:'x'}})` is asserted with toEqual. Legs (b)/(c) run behind the same `BROWSER` gate the file already has.
- `packages/tinyapp-exam/test/render-move.test.ts` — task 2 legs (d) [M4] and (f) [M6].
- `tests/state-exams/click-by-name-completes-todo.test.ts` — leg (g) [M7], the single `stateExam({...})` the leg spells.

One reading I am recording now, because M2's page will not otherwise behave: an empty `<span role=checkbox>` has a zero-area content box, so `DOM.getBoxModel`'s centre is a point no hit test lands on and the click would reach the body. The three elements M2 spells stay byte-identical in the page; the page carries a `<style>` block giving `span[role=checkbox]` a 24x24 inline-block box so a real mouse click can land on it. That changes no action and no name — the span is still named only by `aria-label`.

Leg (e) [M5] names `packages/tinyapp-lint/test/views.test.ts`, which this task's Proof lists under Guard: and not under Test:, and which is not in the run's TEST COMMAND. It is not mine to write; it goes back under `unsatisfiable` and is the implementer's to extend, under a comment naming this task, over the same two-span markup (M5's hand-built LintContext, never `loadContext`).

payload.body:
examiner (exam-3): `tests/lint-ui.test.ts` is in — five tests, one per Proof leg (a)–(e), 35 assertions. Every leg is encoded as written; nothing under `unsatisfiable`.

Red at BASE, each leg for the absent implementation and nothing else:
  (a) `scripts['lint:ui']` is `undefined`;
  (b) `eslint.config.mjs` is not on the tree;
  (c)(d)(e) the guarded parse reports `\`bun run lint:ui -f json\` printed no JSON to parse (exit 1). stdout: "" stderr: "error: Script not found \"lint:ui\""`.

Green on a reference implementation, checked rather than assumed: a scratch copy of this tree with the Proof's verbatim `eslint.config.mjs`, the exact `lint:ui` script and the four devDependencies installed (`@shadcn/lint` 0.1.0, `@typescript-eslint/parser` 8.70.0, `eslint` 10.10.0, `tailwindcss` 4.3.3 — Bun 1.4.0, Node 24.20.0) runs 5 pass / 0 fail in 1.05 s. The scratch copy is gone; this clone carries the exam file and nothing else. Two mutants of that config confirm the exam discriminates: dropping `{ignores: ['client/src/components/ui/**']}` reds leg (d) alone, and spelling `'shadcn/no-restyle': 'error'` without `{allow: ['layout']}` reds leg (b) alone.

Two things the implementer should know about the exam's temporary files. It writes all three — component, sample, ignored copy — under one random suffix, spawns both commands once, and removes them in a `finally`; `client/src/components/` is created only if it was absent and removed again only with `rmdirSync`, which refuses a non-empty directory, so Task 1's real components under `components/ui/` are never at risk. And the exam never pins the exit code of a bare run: only the run with the sample present is pinned to 1, so it is green both at this wave (the app's own seven `no-unknown-classes` findings) and after Task 4.
